extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and USPTO examiners handling patent term extension applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, eligibility rules, filing content, timelines, agency coordination, and calculation rules for U.S. patent term extensions and interim extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156 and implementing CFR/MPEP provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision based on application representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination as to whether a patent is eligible for an extension will normally be made solely from the representations contained in the application for patent term extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require further information or inquiry before a final determination; if further information is required the applicant will be given a time period to respond. Failure to respond within the provided time may result in an adverse final determination unless the period is extended. An intentional failure to provide requested information may result in an adverse final determination. Time period provisions of 37 CFR 1.136 apply to extensions of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of final determination and reconsideration period
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice will be mailed to applicant containing the determination as to eligibility of the patent for extension and the period of time of the extension, if any; this notice shall constitute the final determination as to eligibility and any period of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single request for reconsideration of a final determination may be filed within one month (or other time set in the final determination). If no request for reconsideration is filed within the time period set in the determination, the certificate of patent term extension will be issued. Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not applicable to the usual reconsideration period for Notices of Final Determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension authority (35 U.S.C. 156(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the term of a patent would expire before a certificate of extension is issued or denied, the Director shall extend, until such determination is made, the term of the patent for periods of up to one year if he determines that the patent is eligible for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extensions under this subsection are discretionary, may be issued with or without a request by the applicant, and each interim extension may be for up to one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim-extension request timing and recommended filing window (§1.760)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has filed a formal application for extension may request one or more interim extensions for periods of up to one year each pending a final determination. Any such request should be filed at least three months prior to the expiration date of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month recommendation is not mandatory; requests filed within a shorter period will be considered, upon a proper showing. However, the application for extension, in compliance with 37 CFR 1.741, must have been filed prior to the expiration date of the patent for an interim extension to be granted. Interim extensions will not be longer than the maximum period for extension to which the applicant would be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension publication and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: When an interim extension is granted the patent owner or agent will be notified, and notice of the extension will be published in the Official Gazette; the notice will be recorded in the official file of the patent and will be considered as part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice is treated as part of the original patent; if later determined ineligible the interim extension may be vacated ab initio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension ineligibility and vacatur
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a determination is made that the patent is not eligible for patent term extension, an interim extension of the patent term is not warranted and a previously granted interim extension may be vacated ab initio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Alcon Laboratories, Inc.; In re Reckitt & Colman Products Ltd. — the Office may vacate interim extensions if ultimate ineligibility is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension application content under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for interim extension shall contain the identity of the product subject to regulatory review and the Federal statute under which such review is occurring; identity of the patent and each claim which claims the product or a method of using or manufacturing the product; information to enable the Director to determine eligibility under subsection (a)(1)-(3); a brief description of activities undertaken during the regulatory review period to date and significant dates; and such patent or other information as the Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated items are mandatory content for an interim-extension application under subsection (d)(5)(A)(i)-(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's actions after provisional determination under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines that, except for permission to market or use the product commercially, the patent would be eligible for an extension, the Director shall publish in the Federal Register a notice and shall issue a certificate of interim extension for a period of not more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The owner may apply for subsequent interim extensions (generally up to 4 additional, with special limits for g(6)(C) cases). Each certificate is recorded in the patent file and considered part of the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and conversion of interim extension (35 U.S.C.156(d)(5)(E) and 37 CFR 1.791)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interim extension granted under this paragraph shall terminate at the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date on which the product involved receives permission for commercial marketing or use, except that if within that 60-day period the applicant notifies the Director of such permission and submits any additional information under paragraph (1) not previously contained in the application for interim extension, the patent shall be further extended under the provisions of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, the interim extension ends 60 days after approval unless the owner files a full application (conversion) including any necessary additional information to obtain the full extension under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patent rights during interim extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights derived from any patent the term of which is extended under this paragraph shall, during the period of interim extension, be limited to the use then under regulatory review (if patent claims a product), to the use claimed then under regulatory review (if claims method of use), or to the method of manufacturing as used to make the product then under regulatory review (if claims manufacturing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extension confers narrower rights limited to the subject matter being reviewed; do not assume full patent scope during interim period.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.790 filing windows for interim extensions (initial and subsequent)
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner who reasonably expects regulatory review may submit one or more applications for interim extensions. The initial application must be filed during the period beginning 6 months and ending 15 days before the patent term is due to expire. Each subsequent application must be filed during the period beginning 60 days before and ending 30 days before the expiration of the preceding interim extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extensions granted under this section may not exceed the maximum period of extension to which the applicant would be entitled under 35 U.S.C.156(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application content requirements for interim extension (§1.790(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application for interim extension shall include all of the information required for a formal application under §1.740 and a complete application under §1.741. Sections (a)(1),(a)(2),(a)(4), and (a)(6)-(a)(17) of §1.740 and §1.741 shall be read in the context of a product currently undergoing regulatory review. Sections (a)(3) and (a)(5) of §1.740 are not applicable to an application for interim extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure compliance with the listed portions of §1.740 and §1.741; missing required parts may render the interim application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limitation for subsequent interim-extension applications (§1.790(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of each subsequent interim extension application may be limited to a request for a subsequent interim extension along with a statement that the regulatory review period has not been completed along with any materials or information required under §§1.740 and 1.741 that are not present in the preceding interim extension application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent filings can be streamlined if prior application already contains required materials; include only missing items plus status statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and record maintenance for interim-extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for an application for patent term extension under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(5) is set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(j)(2), and the fee for a subsequent application is set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(j)(3). Copies of an application for interim extension are maintained in the same manner as applications for patent term extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct fee payment per CFR and that copies are retained per USPTO filing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-regulatory agency cooperation and assistance (correspondence procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director decides whether an applicant has satisfied statutory requirements and whether the patent qualifies for extension, but the regulatory agency possesses expertise and records regarding some statutory requirements. The FDA and Department of Agriculture have entered into MOUs with the Office establishing procedures for assistance and exchange of information regarding regulatory review period determinations, due diligence petitions, and informal regulatory agency hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will contact the regulatory agency (usually by sending the application copy) to request information regarding eligibility and, where appropriate, the length of the regulatory review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agency determination of regulatory review period
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory agency is responsible for the determination of the length of the regulatory review period for the approved product on which the application is based. The determination is made based on the application and the agency records for the approved product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory agency publishes the determination in the Federal Register and forwards a letter to the Office containing the total length of the regulatory review period and the relevant dates, separating the total into initial/testing phase and final approval phase. The Federal Register Notice sets a 180-day deadline for filing comments concerning the information or for filing a petition regarding due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content expected in first regulatory-agency reply to Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory agency reply usually verifies whether the product has undergone a regulatory review period within the meaning of 35 U.S.C.156(g); states whether the marketing permission was for the first permitted commercial marketing or use; informs whether the patent term extension application was submitted within sixty days after product approval; and provides any other information relevant to eligibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is compared with the application's related information; if there are no major discrepancies and the patent appears eligible the Office proceeds to request the determination of the regulatory review period length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary eligibility decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of reply from the regulatory agency to the Office's first letter, a preliminary eligibility decision (not final) is made as to whether the patent is eligible for an extension of its term. If eligible (subject to final review), a second letter requesting a determination of the length of the regulatory review period is mailed to the regulatory agency not later than sixty days after the Office receipt date of the agency reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is determined to be ineligible for extension, the Office will dismiss the application rather than request a determination of the regulatory review period (see In re Allen & Hansbury, Ltd.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence petitions procedure and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a due diligence petition is filed during the 180-day period following publication of the regulatory agency determination, the regulatory agency makes the determination under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(2)(B) whether the applicant acted with due diligence during the review. 'Due diligence' is defined in 35 U.S.C.156(d)(3) as 'that degree of attention, continuous directed effort, and timeliness as may reasonably be expected from, and are ordinarily exercised by, a person during a regulatory review period.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the regulatory agency affirms or revises the regulatory review period determination and resolves due diligence petitions/hearings, it notifies the Office and publishes the results in the Federal Register. The regulatory review determination is not final until due diligence petitions and informal hearings, if any, have been resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation formula for period of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of Extension = RRP - PGRRP - DD - 1/2 (TP - PGTP), where 'RRP' is total days in regulatory review period, 'PGRRP' is days of RRP on or before patent issue date, 'DD' is days of RRP when applicant did not act with due diligence, 'TP' is testing phase period, and 'PGTP' is days of TP on or before patent issue date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Half days are ignored in subtraction of 1/2 (TP - PGTP). Only the portion of the regulatory review period occurring after the date the patent issued is considered for extension. No determination of lack of due diligence should be assumed unless found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of pre-issue regulatory-review time and due-diligence subtraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any part of the regulatory review period which occurs before the patent was granted will not be counted toward patent term extension. Any period in which the marketing applicant failed to exercise due diligence, thereby unnecessarily adding to the length of the regulatory review period after the patent issued, will not be considered in determining the length of the extension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office relies on the regulatory agency for due diligence findings; DD days are subtracted in the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory maximum-period limitations and caps (35 U.S.C.156(g)(6), MPEP rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculated extension period is subject to statutory limitations: if the patent's post-approval remaining term plus calculated extension exceeds 14 years, the extension is reduced so the total does not exceed 14 years; calculated extension may not exceed five years for patents issued after the enactment date (or under certain pre-enactment conditions); special limits apply to animal drug/veterinary biological products, including a possible three-year cap in some pre-enactment cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-animal products the caps are (A) 14-year total cap, (B) five-year cap for patents issued after Sept. 24, 1984, (C)-(D) pre-1984 variations. For animal/veterinary products analogous caps include up to three years in certain pre-enactment situations. The Office must apply the appropriate statutory cap in calculating the final extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register publication and 180-day comment/petition window
rubrics_metrics.description: When the regulatory agency determines the regulatory review period it publishes the information in the Federal Register and forwards a letter to the Office; the Federal Register Notice separates total period into testing and approval phases and sets a date 180 days after publication as a deadline for filing written comments or a petition for a due diligence determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and petitions filed within the 180-day window may trigger due diligence proceedings that affect the final regulatory review period and the Office's calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates and issuance (final steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing regulatory agency information, if the Office determines the patent eligible the Office calculates the length of extension and mails a Notice of Final Determination which states the length and the calculations used. In the absence of a timely request for reconsideration, the Director will issue a certificate of extension under seal for the determined period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is ineligible, Notice of Final Determination will set forth the basis for dismissal and the applicant has a period (usually one month) to seek reconsideration. Recently mailed Notices of Final Determination are posted in FOIA section of USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reliance on agency determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will rely on the Secretary’s (or regulatory agency’s) determination of the length of the regulatory review period when calculating the extension; copies of interim-extension applications are maintained similarly to regular patent term extension applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the regulatory agency provides key dates and phase separations, applicants should ensure correspondence and records with the regulatory agency are accurate and complete; misstatements may lead to discrepancies and affect eligibility or calculated extension.
